title: Unleavened flatbread
skill: A dough with no leaven, rolled thin and cooked in a dry pan

notes.2: Makes 12 rounds. Cook them one at a time.

move.title: Bread with no time to rise
move.body: Flour, water, oil, and salt, mixed fast, rolled thin, and cooked in a hot, dry pan. Nothing in it can make it rise, so it bakes flat and crisp.

why.title: Why there's no yeast
why.body: During the Feast of Unleavened Bread, no leaven is eaten for seven days (Leviticus 23:6). When Israel left Egypt, there was no time for the dough to rise, so they baked it flat (Exodus 12:39). This dough has no yeast and no baking powder, so nothing in it makes it puff up.

why.title: Why poke holes
why.body: The water in the dough turns to steam in the hot pan. Holes from a fork let the steam out, so the bread cooks flat and crisp instead of puffing into one big bubble.

why.title: Roll it thin
why.body: Thin dough cooks through in a minute or two and turns crisp. Thick dough stays soft in the middle before the outside is done.

why.title: A hot, dry pan
why.body: No oil goes in the pan. The dry heat browns the spots that touch it and dries the bread out, so it snaps when you break it.

wrong.sign: The dough cracks when you roll it
wrong.fix: It's too dry. Wet your hands and knead the dough for a few seconds.

wrong.sign: The dough sticks to the counter
wrong.fix: Dust the counter and the rolling pin with a little more flour.

wrong.sign: The bread is chewy, not crisp
wrong.fix: Roll the next one thinner, or leave it in the pan a little longer on each side.

quiz.q: Why are there holes poked in the dough?
choices: So it cooks faster in the middle
quiz.explain: Steam from the water in the dough escapes through the holes, so the bread stays flat and crisp.

steps.text: Stir the flour and salt together in the bowl. Pour in the oil and water, and stir until it comes together into a rough dough.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. Raw flour can make you sick.

steps.text: Dust the counter with flour. Knead the dough until it's smooth.
steps.tip: Go straight on to the next steps. This dough doesn't need to rest.

steps.text: Divide the dough into balls about the size of a golf ball.
Put the skillet over medium-high heat, with nothing in it.
Roll one ball out as thin as you can, about 8 inches across. Prick it all over with the fork.
steps.tip: If it shrinks back, let it sit for a minute, then roll again.

steps.text: Lay the round in the dry pan. Cook it until brown spots show underneath, then flip it with the spatula and cook the other side.
steps.look: Brown spots on both sides, and it feels dry and stiff.

steps.text: Move it to the plate. Roll, prick, and cook the rest the same way.
Turn off the heat. Let the rounds cool on the plate. They get crisper as they cool.
